title: Spooky Maryland attractions that won’t scare the hell out of kids
text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Spooky Maryland attractions that won’t scare the hell out of kids

These attractions and events across Maryland allow kids to participate without the risk of getting too frightened.

Actual Article Body:
Jack-o’-lanterns are gearing up for creepy, snaggletoothed smiles, pumpkin spice lattes galore are on the horizon and haunted houses are dusting off their doorsteps.

Fall is here along with the spooky season when countless kiddos and adults will test their courage at haunted attractions or run for the hills. But Halloween-leaning fun doesn’t have to be synonymous with bed-wetting fear.

Little tykes still have a chance to get in on the entertainment whether simply dressing up at an event or exploring a corn maze.

These attractions and events across Maryland allow kids to participate without the risk of getting too scared.

Attendees at the ZooBOO! Festival, which kicks off Friday, are encouraged to wear family-friendly costumes while participating in mostly free activities throughout the Maryland Zoo. There will be face painting, sack races, costume contests on Saturdays and Sundays, and food trucks and vendors.

ZooBOO!, which takes place most weekends in October, is included with the price of zoo admission or a membership. Children under 2 are free. Tickets range from $28 to $33.

The Maryland Zoo is located at 1 Safari Place in Baltimore.

Survival isn’t guaranteed at the Terror Trail in Davidsonville, which is recommended for courageous kids over 8 years old. The Boo Loop, where no one will jump out, is designed for the younger kids, with static displays and a scavenger hunt with prizes. These offerings are only open Fridays and Saturdays throughout October. Attendees are invited to dress up as they enjoy the attractions and food truck.

Terror Trail tickets are $30 and Boo Loop tickets cost $10. Proceeds support the Arundel Volunteer Fire Department Station 7, and ticket discounts are available to first responders, teachers, veterans, medical professionals and those who bring a canned food item.

The AVFD Station 7 Terror Trail is located at 2701 Davidsonville Road in Davidsonville.

Until Nov. 8, families can head to Weber’s Cider Mill Farm in Parkville to experience all things fall with a smidge of spooky, including a family-friendly skeleton walk, a hay maze, farm animals and play structures. For an additional cost, kids can have their faces painted or get a glitter tattoo. And for your fall food fill, apple cider donuts, apple slushies and more are on the menu.

Tickets are required for anyone 2 years old and up. Weekday festival admission starts at $12, while the weekend costs $15. Or you can get unlimited entry on weekdays with a season pass that’ll run you $35. Admission pricing is subject to change throughout the season.

Weber’s Cider Mill Farm is located at 2526 Proctor Lane in Parkville.

For a controlled encounter with the dead, the Burying Ground at Westminster Hall is usually open daily for self-guided tours from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., according to Westminster Hall’s website. Edgar Allan Poe’s large marble grave site is a popular stop within the grounds. There are also catacombs that can only be explored through a guided tour.

For $5 a person, Westminster Hall is hosting a catacombs tour on Oct. 31 from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. Baltimore Heritage also provides a tour of the catacombs for $10-$15.

Westminster Hall and Burying Grounds are located at 551 W. Fayette St. in Baltimore.

Baltimore City Recreation and Parks is offering an opportunity to drive through terror on Oct. 16 from 7 p.m. to 10 p.m. Pack the kiddos in the car, choose your time slot and schedule a date with horror as a portion of the 745-acre Druid Hill Park is turned into a roadway of doom. The event is open to all ages, and there are subtle ways to maximize or minimize the scares.

For an intense, scary experience, keep the doors unlocked and the windows down. For a less frightening time, make sure to do the opposite. Keep at least a half-gallon of gas in your tank since you’ll have to wait in line in your car to enter.

Each car costs $13.

Druid Hill Park is located at 3001 E. Drive in Baltimore.
